text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.69% today to close at $424.89, extending a strong two-week rally of nearly 10%. The stock has climbed steadily since mid-September as oil prices have remained elevated—U.S. crude is trading at $107 per barrel while global oil sits at $130.80—and refineries are running at 96.8% capacity. With diesel and heating oil inventories at historically tight levels (107.9 million barrels) and record diesel prices pushing through the U.S. transportation system, refinery operators like Marathon benefit from both higher crude values and strong margins on fuel products they process and sell.

The Middle East tensions that earlier in the week had threatened supply disruptions have been largely priced in after Saudi Arabia signaled it would increase exports to offset pipeline damage, calming immediate supply-shock fears. This has allowed the oil market to stabilize at elevated levels rather than spike further—a scenario that actually favors refiners, who profit most when crude and product prices find a sustainable middle ground rather than when volatility spikes in either direction.
